_readme: THE COUNTER'S MENU, AS DATA — the totem's store, its four menu bands, and the fifteen products the
counter sells that nothing else in this instance sells. `seed/totem.mjs` reads this file and drives the
port; nothing here is code, and no rule about a product lives in the module.
IT IS THE SIBLING OF `seed/catalog.json`, deliberately — same money-in-cents, same `options`/`skus`
shape, same `custom_fields` bag — so a merchant who has read one can edit the other. What it adds is the
half a single-store catalogue never needed: a `category` per product, and a list of products it does NOT
create but PUBLISHES (`publish_also`).
MONEY IS IN CENTS, always, and never a float. `amount: 1350` is R$ 13,50.
★ THE DELTA BETWEEN SIZES IS A PRICE PER SKU AND NEVER A CALCULATION. A cappuccino G with oat milk is
one row with one number, not `base + size + milk`. The moment a delta is arithmetic, the shop can no
longer be re-priced by a person editing a file — which is the whole reason this file exists.
★ THE OPTION VALUES ARE THE PROTOTYPE'S OWN STRINGS ('P 200ml', 'Com tônica e limão', 'Porção c/ 3') and
not dry letters. The totem prints them on the chips, so they are copy, and fidelity to the prototype is a
mandate. ⚠️ AND THEY TRAVEL: an order line freezes its option values, so the admin's order screen reads
'Cappuccino · G · Aveia' from exactly these words. Renaming one later does not rewrite an order already
placed.
⚠️ THE CATEGORY `path` IS NOT THE HANDLE, FOR ONE OF THE FOUR, AND THE KERNEL IS WHY. A category path is
an ltree label path — `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, dots between labels (packages/core/src/commands/catalog.ts, the
`ltreePathFloor` regex, with `::ltree` itself as the authority behind it). A hyphen is refused. So the
frozen handle `pra-levar` keeps its hyphen and its PATH is `pra_levar`, which is what a reader filtering
the menu passes to `read.products?store=…&category=…`. The other three spell the same either way.
⚠️ `tag_balcao` IS THE SEAL ON THE CARD, AND IT IS DATA — the prototype carries one per product. What is
NOT here is its COLOUR: the prototype derives that from the tag itself in its view builder, so the colour
belongs to the totem app and the word belongs to the product. One word, one owner.
⚠️ THE SIX COFFEES AND THE MUG ARE IN `publish_also` AND NOT IN `products`, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE
WHOLE FILE. They already exist — `seed/catalog.json` created them for the coffee shop. Re-creating them
here would be a second product with a second price to keep equal by hand; publishing them into a second
store is one command, and the price the counter charges is then the SAME SKU the e-commerce sells. (The
mug is the exception that proves it: it is new, so it is in `products` AND listed for the `pra-levar`
band.)

store.name: Forge Café · Balcão
store.why: The counter of the same coffee shop, on the same tenant — a second STORE and not a second tenant, because the whole demonstration is one catalogue serving two assortments. No `theme_key`: the totem is an app of its own and resolves no theme, so a theme key here would be a promise nothing keeps.

categories.name: Cafés
categories.why: The four bands of the menu are KERNEL CATEGORIES and not a field of this file, so the totem reads the menu with the mechanism every other reader already has (`read.products?category=…`, `read.category_paths`). ⚠️ They are TENANT-wide — `catalog.category.create` takes no store — so what answers 'which of these does the COUNTER fill?' is `read.category_paths?store=<balcao>`, never this list.

categories.name: Pra levar
categories.why: The path may not carry the handle's hyphen — ltree refuses it. See the readme above.

_categories_order_why: The order of this list is the order of the menu strip. The kernel has no position on a category, so a reader that wants the merchant's order reads it from here or sorts by name; `read.categories` answers a MAP and a map has none.

custom_fields.label: Café da semana
custom_fields.why: The thread that ties the counter to the retail shelf. The menu promises the pour-over is 'made with this week's coffee', and this holds the HANDLE of one of the six the e-commerce sells — so changing the week is editing one word in this file, not re-writing a description. Declared before any product writes it: an undeclared key is accepted and then read by nobody.

custom_fields.label: Selo do balcão
custom_fields.why: The word on the seal over the photograph ('quente', 'gelado', 'do forno'…). It is on the PRODUCT and not in the totem's source so the merchant can change it from the admin, and so the seed and the app cannot drift into two vocabularies.

custom_fields.label: Descrição do totem
custom_fields.why: A48 — THE COUNTER'S OWN ONE-LINER, and the cleanest example in this instance of trava 3 (dado novo → campo próprio). The scrolling card is a tile on a screen a metre away; the shop's paragraph is written for a product page you read sitting down. One product, one price, one kernel — and each surface chooses what to read: the TOTEM's card prefers this, the totem's MODAL keeps the short description, and the coffee shop's vitrine never asks for it and sees no difference. No kernel change, no contract, no new surface. ⚠️ It is OPTIONAL by design: a product without it falls back to `description`, so the field is an upgrade and never a requirement — see `totem/src/lib/menu.ts`.

_custom_fields_why: Portuguese keys, like `regiao`/`torra`/`notas` in seed/catalog.json. These are a merchant's vocabulary in a Brazilian shop's admin, not identifiers of this repository's code — the code around them is English, as the house rule says.

products._skus_why: Two flavours at the SAME price, written twice rather than as one SKU with a note. The axis is what the shopper picks and the order line has to freeze which slice was sold — a single SKU would sell 'a cake' and the counter would not know which one to hand over.

products.title: Caneca esmaltada forge.co
products._why: The one NEW product of the 'pra levar' band, and the only one here with no axis at all: a mug is a mug. Its stock is a real count (40) and not the drinks' figure — see `default_on_hand` below.

publish_also.why: MULTISTORE, in one list. These six are NOT created here: they are the e-commerce's own products, put on sale in a second store and filed under the counter's 'Pra levar' band. The price the totem prints is the same SKU the shop sells, live from the kernel — which is the thing that cannot be faked by a second catalogue.

publish_also._desc_totem_why: A48 — the counter's own one-liner for the six coffees, and the ONLY items that needed one: their `description` is the shop's paragraph (200+ characters, written for a product page) and on a card a metre away it ran over the tile. The counter's fifteen own products already carry a one-line description, so they are DELIBERATELY absent here — the fallback in `totem/src/lib/menu.ts` shows their `description` unchanged, which is what makes this field an upgrade instead of a requirement, and what puts the fallback under a customer's eyes on the bench rather than only under a test's. ⚠️ Written by MERGE, like the seal: see `_tags_why`.
publish_also._tags_why: The seal each of the six wears on the totem's card. Writing it means EDITING a product of the coffee shop, so `seed/totem.mjs` merges it into the metadata it reads rather than replacing the bag — `catalog.product.update` replaces `metadata` wholesale, and a replacement here would erase `regiao`/`torra`/`notas`/`sca`.

_stock_why: ★ THE DRINKS' 'KEEP SELLING' POLICY, AND WHY IT IS A BIG NUMBER RATHER THAN THE POLICY ITSELF.
The menu says a counter drink is made to order and never sells out. The kernel HAS that idea, and it is
called `oversell_policy: 'allow'` — but it lives on the WAREHOUSE (packages/core/src/commands/inventory.ts,
`warehouse.create`/`warehouse.update`), never on a SKU or a product.
⚠️ AND IT IS NOT SCOPED BY WHAT THE WAREHOUSE STOCKS, which is what makes a second 'counter warehouse'
the wrong answer rather than a clever one. The router's candidate set is `cross join warehouse where
active` (packages/core/src/inventory/purchasable.ts) — EVERY active warehouse is a candidate for EVERY
sku, with `available: 0` where it has never counted one — and its second pass is 'nobody covers the line
and some active warehouse allows overselling → backorder there' (packages/core/src/inventory/routing.ts).
So one warehouse set to `allow` makes every SKU OF THE TENANT sellable past zero, the six retail coffees
of the e-commerce included. That is a decision about the whole shop and not about the counter's milk.
So: this bench's single warehouse stays on `block`, and the drinks carry a stock figure large enough that
the counter never runs out. It is honest about what it is — a number, not a policy — and it is written
here rather than in the module so it can be raised without touching code.

location.name: Balcão · Forge Café
location.instructions: Retire no balcão quando chamarmos o seu nome.

why: ★ THE COUNTER DOES NOT DELIVER, AND `checkout.place_order` STILL DEMANDS A SHIPPING METHOD.
Its completeness check lists `buyer`, `shipping_method` and `payment_method`
(packages/core/src/commands/checkout.ts), so an order placed at a totem needs a method like any other.
The honest one is RETRIEVAL: the kernel has a method KIND for it (`pickup`, in
packages/core/src/commands/shipping.ts) and a pickup POINT to go with it
(`pickup_location.create`), and the order then freezes the point's name, address and instructions —
which is exactly what 'retire no balcão quando chamarmos' means, said in the kernel's own words.
⚠️ SHIPPING CONFIG IS TENANT-WIDE, NOT PER STORE. Neither `shipping.method.create` nor
`shipping.zone.create` nor `pickup_location.create` takes a `store_id` — measured against the source
and against this bench, where the whole tenant had ZERO methods, zones, rates and points before this
seed. So this pickup option appears in the coffee shop's and the outlet's checkouts too. It is
additive (there was nothing to displace) and it is honest (it is the same shop), but it is a fact
about the TENANT that a file about the counter had better say out loud.
⚠️ AND THE ADDRESS IS STILL REQUIRED. Choosing a pickup method does NOT exempt a cart from carrying a
shipping address: the completeness check asks for `ship_line1`/`city`/`region`/`postal_code`/
`country_code` on any cart nobody is recognized on, pickup or not. The address above is therefore the
one the totem sends — the counter's own — so the order says the shop's address rather than a fiction.
Note it goes through `cart.set_delivery`; `cart.set_buyer` carries only e-mail, name, tax id and phone.
The zone spans every Brazilian postal code because a retrieval has no destination to price: the
shopper comes here. Price 0, window 0–0 days, one weight bracket wide enough that no basket misses it.
★★ THE WEEK, AND WHY IT IS WRITTEN OUT. Until 05/09 this object had no `hours` key, and the consequence
was photographed on the screen: the checkout's pickup card listed the seven days as «Fechado» and its
today-line said «Fechado hoje». That was not a rendering defect — an OMITTED day is closed to the
kernel, exactly like a `null` one (`pickupHoursSchema`, packages/core/src/shipping/pickup.ts), so a
point with no week is stored, is valid, and is a shop nobody can ever collect from. The four points of
`seed/logistics.json` had written all seven days since A22; this one had written none, and nothing
could tell that apart from a counter that is genuinely shut. `seed/pickup-hours.mjs` is the rule that
now refuses the ambiguity, and `bin/verify-seed.mjs` asks it of the live box, by name, per point.
★ MEASURED ON THE BENCH OF 05/09, and the two ends spell it differently: the FILE had no key at all,
while the create handler writes `JSON.stringify(input.hours ?? {})` — so the row read back
`Balcão · Forge Café | {}` while the shoe brand's four each read back a full week. An empty week and an
absent one are the same shop, which is why the rule below refuses both.
THE HOURS ARE A VILA MADALENA CAFÉ'S, not a nine-to-five with the weekend off. It opens at 08:00 on
the way to work and closes at 19:00 at the start of the week; it stretches to 22:00 on Thursday and
23:00 on Friday and Saturday, when the neighbourhood fills up and the counter is the reason people are
on Fradique Coutinho at that hour; and Sunday is brunch — 09:00 to 17:00, because Sunday evening here
belongs to the bars and not to a coffee counter. Seven days written, none of them `null`: a café of
this street does not close for a whole day, and the file says so rather than leaving it to be guessed.
⚠️ NOTHING CROSSES MIDNIGHT. The kernel refuses `open >= close`, so a counter serving past 00:00 would
need two registers and not a night shift — none is written, and that is the kernel's cut, not a gap.
⚠️ AND THE WEEK IS TENANT-WIDE LIKE THE POINT ITSELF. `pickup_location.create` takes no `store_id`, so
these hours are the ones the coffee shop's checkout shows too — the same door, said once. The trade-off,
stated: the TOTEM does not care — it never consumes this information — but the COFFEE SHOP has every
reason to carry it.
⚠️ IT IS BORN WITH THE POINT, AND ONLY THEN. This step is idempotent BY NAME (so is `seedLogistics`):
a box that already holds «Balcão · Forge Café» is left alone, hours or no hours. On a bench seeded
before this date the week arrives with the next birth, never with a re-run — which is why the check
lives in `bin/verify-seed.mjs`, where a stale box is a ✗ with the point's name in it.

coupon.name: Primeiro café 10%
coupon.label: PRIMEIROCAFE · 10% OFF
coupon.why: ★ SCOPED TO THE COUNTER by `store_id`, which is what the DoD asks to be proven. ⚠️ MEASURE WHAT 'does not work in the coffee shop' ACTUALLY MEANS: `cart.apply_coupon` does not filter by store (packages/core/src/commands/coupon.ts resolves the code and only asks whether the cart holds something the TARGET covers), while the pricing engine does (packages/core/src/promo/context.ts — `p.store_id is null or p.store_id = $n`). So the same code on a coffee-shop cart is ACCEPTED and discounts NOTHING. It is scoped; it is not refused.

combo.name: Combo da manhã
combo.label: Combo da manhã · R$ 3,00 OFF
combo.why: 'Cart contains' is a CONDITION and the kernel spells it exactly (`cart_contains`, packages/contracts/src/promotion.ts): EVERY product listed must be in the cart — which is what a combo means, and not 'any of', which is what a target already expresses. The benefit is a FIXED AMOUNT and not a percentage because a totem screen has one line to explain itself: 'R$ 3,00 OFF' is a number a person checks against the total, while '12%' is arithmetic they have to trust. ⚠️ It is created AFTER the products: the condition names product IDs, so the targets have to exist first.
